paper-2501.09223.title: Foundations of Large Language Models
paper-2501.09223.summary: This is a book about large language models. As indicated by the title, it primarily focuses on foundational concepts rather than comprehensive coverage of all cutting-edge technologies.

paper-2602.05758.title: LongR: Unleashing Long-Context Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning with Dense Utility Rewards
paper-2602.05758.summary: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has emerged as a key driver for LLM reasoning.

paper-2605.09742.title: TIDES: Implicit Time-Awareness in Selective State Space Models
paper-2605.09742.summary: Selective state space models (SSMs), such as Mamba, achieve strong per-token expressivity by making the time discretization step TildeΔ a learned function of the input.

paper-2605.16817.title: Adaptive Fused Prior Transfer for Controllable Generative Image Compression
paper-2605.16817.summary: Learned image compression achieves competitive rate-distortion performance, but very-low-bitrate reconstruction remains challenging because the transmitted representation cannot preserve fine textures and local structures.

paper-2605.21318.title: TextReg: Mitigating Prompt Distributional Overfitting via Regularized Text-Space Optimization
paper-2605.21318.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are highly sensitive to the prompts used to specify task objectives and behavioral constraints.

paper-2605.22493.title: Understanding Multimodality in Generative Behavioral Cloning
paper-2605.22493.summary: Behavioral cloning becomes challenging when the same observation admits several valid actions. We study how generative behavioral-cloning policies represent such multimodal expert behavior and identify different bottlenecks across model parameterizations.

paper-2605.22949.title: MARGIN: Runtime Confidence Calibration for Multi-Agent Foundation Model Coordination
paper-2605.22949.summary: When a coordinator compares answers from heterogeneous foundation models, self-reported confidence may have different meanings across responders and changing workloads.

paper-2606.03335.title: A GPU-Parallel Framework for Heterogeneous Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning
paper-2606.03335.summary: GPU-parallel simulation provides abundant robot interaction, but existing benchmarks rarely combine this scale with heterogeneous manipulation tasks and standardized multi-task RL evaluation.

paper-2606.10953.title: Architect-Ant: Editable Automatic Furnishing of Architectural Floor Plans
paper-2606.10953.summary: Furnished floor plans support real-estate visualization, interior design, and architectural workflows, yet automatic furnishing remains challenged by limited real-world data and the need to satisfy interacting geometric and functional constraints.

paper-2606.24472.title: G^3VLA: Geometric Inductive Bias for Vision-Language-Action Models
paper-2606.24472.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have rapidly advanced generalist robot manipulation by harnessing the semantic knowledge of pretrained vision-language backbones.

paper-2607.08809.title: Privacy-Preserving Intent Fulfilment and Assurance for 6G RAN
paper-2607.08809.summary: Intent-based network management automates 6G service lifecycles, but existing fulfilment and assurance approaches require traffic inspection, per-flow tracking, or vendor-internal telemetry.

paper-2608.26762.title: Equal Ranking Quality, Different Decisions: Measuring and Reducing Order Dependence in LLM Scorers
paper-2608.26762.summary: In passage reranking, response ranking and multi-document question answering, LLMs can score several candidate documents or responses together in one prompt, each still receiving its own score.

paper-2609.13730.title: JumpStart Your Policy Learning with Lessons from 160,000 Training Runs
paper-2609.13730.summary: Reliable progress in offline policy learning depends on careful reporting, well-tuned baselines, and evaluation across diverse conditions.

paper-2609.18587.title: Label-free steering: Compressing test-time reinforcement learning into bias-only subspaces
paper-2609.18587.summary: Test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL) enables models to improve their reasoning without relying on labeled training data, but existing approaches typically optimize a large fraction of the model parameters.

paper-2609.22753.title: Replacing Large Language Models with Jev Decision Models for Low-Latency Edge Service Orchestration
paper-2609.22753.summary: Natural-language service requests can require a language-model decision before execution starts, consuming part of the request's latency budget.

paper-2609.23136.title: Intent Interpretation at RIC Timescales: Jev Decision Models versus Large Language Models in 6G Open RAN
paper-2609.23136.summary: Intent-based Open RAN needs an interpreter that turns intents into A1 policies within the loop of the RAN intelligent controller (RIC).

paper-2609.24555.title: The Endless Exam: Mathematical Constructions from Today's Models toward Superintelligence
paper-2609.24555.summary: We introduce the Endless Exam, a benchmark spanning fourteen parameterised families of mathematical construction problems, with verifiable scores that distinguish progress before and beyond published mathematical frontiers.

paper-2609.24890.title: OSWorld-Pro: Process-based Evaluation for Computer Use Agents
paper-2609.24890.summary: Evaluation of Computer-Use Agents (CUAs) is often limited to the final deliverables they create (at the end of hundreds of steps) and assessed with functional verifiers, as seen in OSWorld.

paper-2609.26425.title: QuantWM: Temporally Consistent 2-Bit KV Cache Quantization for Video World Models
paper-2609.26425.summary: Video world models achieve long-range temporal consistency by storing KV cache during generation, but the growing cache makes KV cache memory a major deployment bottleneck, which motivates low-bit quantization study for efficiency.

paper-2609.26590.title: GTR: Gated Token Recurrence for Efficient Dense Prediction
paper-2609.26590.summary: Self-attention-based vision backbones perform well on dense prediction, but the quadratic computational cost of global softmax attention limits their efficiency as image resolution increases.

paper-2609.28339.title: Beyond Future Prediction: Denoising as Generative Adaptation for Robot Control
paper-2609.28339.summary: Pretrained generative Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) capture rich pixel-level visual and language-conditioned structure through large-scale image and video generation training.

paper-2609.29123.title: Accent Analogy Guidance: More Speaker Similarity at Equal Accent in Cross-Lingual Voice Cloning
paper-2609.29123.summary: In cross-lingual zero-shot text-to-speech, the accent of the reference leaks into the target speech.

paper-2609.29142.title: Not Every Token Is Worth Distilling: Selective Supervision for Direct-OPD
paper-2609.29142.summary: Direct On-Policy Distillation (Direct-OPD) transfers reinforcement-learning-induced policy improvements from a small model to a larger student by using the token-level log-ratio between post-RL and pre-RL checkpoints as dense supervision on the student's own…

paper-2609.29792.title: TimeBraid: Unifying Time Series and Language for Understanding and Forecasting
paper-2609.29792.summary: We present TimeBraid, a series of unified time-series and language models that align pretrained language models and pretrained time-series foundation models through interleaved global residual attention layers.

paper-2609.30467.title: Where Does Retrieval-Based Open-Ended Evaluation Fail? Automatic Taxonomy Induction from Long-Form Medical Answer Factuality Verification
paper-2609.30467.summary: Retrieval-based factuality evaluation, where LLM-generated claims are verified against evidence from authoritative medical corpora, has become the dominant paradigm for scalable hallucination detection in high-stakes clinical settings.

paper-2609.30541.title: AutoResearch at Production Scale: Failure Modes and a Multi-Agent Framework
paper-2609.30541.summary: Optimizing embedding systems for production recommendation pipelines demands systematic exploration that consumes disproportionate engineering effort at scale.

paper-2609.30840.title: Aligning One-Step Generative Models with Reward-Weighted Transport Distillation
paper-2609.30840.summary: One-step generators enable high-quality visual generation with a single network evaluation, but their post-training is difficult: general implicit generators provide neither tractable likelihoods nor denoising trajectories, and many rewards are non-differenti…

paper-2609.31507.title: SatNav: A Scalable Benchmark for Long-Horizon UAV Vision-Language Navigation from Satellite Imagery
paper-2609.31507.summary: Urban uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) vision-language navigation (VLN) requires agents to follow instructions across extended urban spaces, inherently demanding long-term memory and geospatial grounding.

paper-2609.31662.title: Learning Steadily: Accumulating Relative Point Margin Scores for Face Image Quality Assessment
paper-2609.31662.summary: Face Image Quality Assessment determines the suitability of captured face images for automated face recognition (FR), a critical capability for reliable biometric systems.

paper-2609.32019.title: Decentralized Master-Mind: Joint Action Refinement through Iterative Intent Denoising in Multi-Agent Pathfinding
paper-2609.32019.summary: Decentralized multi-agent path finding (MAPF) with communication requires agents to reach individual goals without collisions under partial observability. Learnable policies trained on expert data provide an effective approach to this problem.

paper-2609.32046.title: Receiver-Conditioned Latent Communication gives 94% CacheBack
paper-2609.32046.summary: Multi-agent systems distribute large contexts across agents that communicate to solve a task. Text messages are compact but require decoding and may omit evidence the receiving agent needs. Recent latent communication instead transfers KV caches.

paper-2609.32182.title: KeyRec: Bounded Visual Memory for Streaming and Long-Video Understanding
paper-2609.32182.summary: Vision-language models are increasingly used to understand long videos and continuous streams. However, dense visual tokens accumulate with video duration, making long-context inference prohibitively expensive.

paper-2609.32259.title: Prefill-Free Cross-Family KV Cache Transfer for Heterogeneous Multi-Agent LLMs
paper-2609.32259.summary: Recent multi-agent LLM systems increasingly combine heterogeneous models for specialized agent roles. However, text-based communication requires each receiver to prefill shared context already processed by the sender.

paper-2609.32264.title: LANTERN: Illuminating Hidden Mathematical Knowledge in Language Models
paper-2609.32264.summary: Language models can now prove theorems, but people still decide which problems to pursue. We ask whether a model's internal representations can help identify promising mathematical connections.

paper-2609.32423.title: PluginRSI: Recursive Improvement of Agent Harnesses with Reusable Plugins
paper-2609.32423.summary: The harness surrounding a language model is a central determinant of agent performance. Recent methods optimize harnesses by searching over complete programs, where individual mechanisms are difficult to isolate and reuse.

paper-2609.32510.title: GeoCR: Learning a Generalist Cloud Removal Prior from Heterogeneous Observations
paper-2609.32510.summary: Cloud removal methods are typically specialized to individual datasets and input configurations, limiting reuse across sensors, spectral bands, and observation settings.

paper-2609.32520.title: When Users Change Their Minds: Measuring and Repairing Intent Drift in LLM Agents
paper-2609.32520.summary: LLM agents often operate over multi-turn interactions in which user intent changes before execution. We study intent drift: the failure mode in which superseded parts of the user's intent continue to influence the final answer or tool action.

paper-2609.32536.title: Do Audio LLMs Listen Before They Act? Diagnosing Acoustic-Context Gating in Voice Agents
paper-2609.32536.summary: Audio language models can recognize spoken commands and invoke tools, but an agent must first decide whether the acoustic and conversational context warrants action.

paper-2609.32600.title: CUA-SWE: When Computer-Use Agents Meet Visual Software Engineering
paper-2609.32600.summary: Software development requires more than editing code: developers repeatedly run software, interact with its interfaces, visually inspect its behavior, and use these observations to decide what to change next and whether a change works.

paper-2609.32720.title: BiasReducer: Adaptive Bias Mitigation for Reward Models
paper-2609.32720.summary: Reward models score responses from large language models (LLMs) and guide LLM training toward human preferences.

paper-2609.32759.title: The Extender: A Log-Structured Transformer
paper-2609.32759.summary: We introduce the Extender, a log-structured variant of the standard Transformer architecture. In a standard Transformer, each layer communicates with subsequent layers exclusively via the residual h, a superposition channel.

paper-2609.32777.title: DEFINE: Exemplar-Guided Accent Control for Zero-Shot TTS
paper-2609.32777.summary: Zero-shot text-to-speech (TTS) can reproduce an unseen speaker from a short reference recording, but typically entangles speaker identity and accent within the same reference.

paper-2609.32810.title: OpenTumorBoard: A Real-World Benchmark of Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Discussion Trajectories
paper-2609.32810.summary: Multidisciplinary tumor boards integrate multimodal clinical observations and longitudinal patient histories through specialist discussions, yet benchmarks rarely capture these real-world trajectories.

paper-2609.32921.title: Adaptive Latent Capacity for World Models
paper-2609.32921.summary: We introduce Adaptive LeWorldModel (ALeWM), a world model based on a joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) that learns to concentrate predictive information in compact prefixes of a wide latent representation.

paper-2609.32993.title: X-Tree: Tokenizing Reusable Experience for Efficient Agent Generalization
paper-2609.32993.summary: Multi-step agents are trained on flat action streams: SFT and RLVR weight every token uniformly and ignore the sub-procedures that recur across tasks, the hierarchy that lets humans plan top-down from reusable routines.

paper-2609.33304.title: Relevance Does Not Imply Applicability: Experience Activation for Personal GUI Agents
paper-2609.33304.summary: Personal Graphical User Interface (GUI) agents rely on interaction history to infer what a user wants from ambiguous instructions and to anticipate recurring routines.

paper-2609.33355.title: Unmask the State: When Does State Adaptation Matter for Masked Diffusion Language Models
paper-2609.33355.summary: Masked diffusion language models (MDMs) admit flexible generation orders, making the unmasking strategy an inference decision.

paper-2609.33403.title: DataMagic: Authoring Data Videos through Declarative Multi-Agent Orchestration
paper-2609.33403.summary: Data videos communicate data insights through dynamic charts, voice narration, and synchronized animations, and have become a widely adopted form of data storytelling.

paper-2609.33463.title: Rethinking Token Reweighting for SFT: Suppress, Reverse, and Extrapolate Learned Features
paper-2609.33463.summary: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) learns most aggressively from tokens that the model deems least likely. This helps acquire new behaviors, but also amplifies noisy or conflicting supervision and can overwrite useful pretrained knowledge.

paper-2609.33659.title: Learning Multimodal Embeddings with Evidence-Aligned Readout
paper-2609.33659.summary: Multimodal large language models can expose task-relevant evidence through generation, but producing useful evidence does not by itself determine how it enters a retrieval embedding.

paper-2609.33678.title: SWE-Game: Can Coding Agents Build the Games We Want?
paper-2609.33678.summary: We introduce SWE-Game, a benchmark of 247 tasks grounded in 41 executable reference Godot games spanning 13 gameplay categories in 2D and 3D.

paper-2609.33711.title: DuoOPD: Learning from Joint Teacher-Student Outcomes for Multi-Task On-Policy Distillation
paper-2609.33711.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student on its own responses with token-level feedback from a stronger teacher, yet the teacher can fail on questions the student already answers correctly, and how often each model succeeds varies across tasks.

paper-2609.33804.title: MinkowskiPE: Minkowski Positional Encoding for Spatiotemporal Perception
paper-2609.33804.summary: Modeling spatiotemporal coupling is a key challenge in building physical intelligence across scales, from microscopic to macroscopic.

paper-2609.33987.title: Opera: A Verbal Critic Framework for Long-horizon Coding Agents
paper-2609.33987.summary: Long-horizon coding agents need timely corrections, yet feedback can be ineffective or even harmful when it misjudges ongoing work or fails to address the underlying problem.

paper-2609.34117.title: SlimWise: Decoupling Expert Pruning Across Prefill and Decode for Efficient MoE Serving
paper-2609.34117.summary: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) models activate few experts per token, yet batched decoding can access nearly the entire expert pool, making expert-weight traffic a major bottleneck.

paper-2609.34162.title: SlideDP: Scaling Host-Resident LLM Fine-Tuning Across Multiple GPUs
paper-2609.34162.summary: Host-resident layer streaming enables full-parameter LLM fine-tuning beyond GPU memory, but data-parallel ranks compete for shared host resources. Replicated transfers amplify traffic, while strong scaling can expose host work as computation windows shrink.

paper-2609.34210.title: RLE-Bench: A Qualifying Exam for Coding Agents as Robot Learning Engineers
paper-2609.34210.summary: Coding agents are beginning to move beyond purely digital tasks to tackle physical-world challenges, particularly in robotics.

paper-2609.34227.title: When Does Selection Replace Extraction? A Pre-Registered Test of Agent Memory with a Typed Decision Model
paper-2609.34227.summary: Does conversational memory need LLM-extracted facts, or is selecting the right raw turns enough? Published results disagree. Extraction-based systems report gains from distilled facts.

paper-2609.34274.title: BIABench: Evaluating AI agents on real-world bioimage analysis tasks
paper-2609.34274.summary: Artificial-intelligence (AI) agents hold promise for automating bioimage analysis, yet no benchmark evaluates whether they can carry out real-world analyses end to end.

paper-2609.34276.title: NavHarness: Towards Lifelong Embodied Navigation
paper-2609.34276.summary: Frontier models can now perform well on individual embodied navigation tasks through multi-round multimodal reasoning with simple tools.

paper-2609.34344.title: Learning to Steer, Steering to See: Unveiling the Geometry of RLVR in Large Language Models via Trainable Vectors
paper-2609.34344.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a key paradigm for enhancing the reasoning of large language models, yet the high dimensionality of parameter updates makes its training dynamics hard to analyze.

paper-2609.34381.title: Joint and Cross-Modal Video-Audio Generation and Editing: A Unified Formulation and Design Taxonomy
paper-2609.34381.summary: Video and audio are perceived together, yet most generative models treat them in isolation.

paper-2609.34563.title: Rethinking Latent Visual Reasoning: Grounding Latent Reasoning in Visual Evidence
paper-2609.34563.summary: Latent visual reasoning (LVR) enables multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to perform intermediate computation in continuous latent tokens rather than expressing every reasoning step in words.

paper-2609.34599.title: The Low-Rank Structure of VLA Reinforcement Learning
paper-2609.34599.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) is increasingly used to post-train vision-language-action (VLA) models, yet how RL reshapes these policies remains poorly understood.

paper-2609.34621.title: Does Native 3D Texture Generation Necessarily Require 3D Assets for Training?
paper-2609.34621.summary: Native 3D texture generation synthesizes colors directly in 3D space for a given geometry, conditioned on multi-view reference images.

paper-2609.34677.title: Learning What to Recall: Adaptive Multi-Cue Episodic Memory for World Models
paper-2609.34677.summary: World models predict future observations from current experience and actions, yet prediction can depend on observations seen far in the past.

paper-2609.34715.title: PDE-JEPA: Predictive Representation Learning of Latent Dynamics Modeling for Parametric PDEs
paper-2609.34715.summary: Physical trajectories contain more than snapshots of a system: they also reveal how its states evolve under governing conditions.

paper-2609.34736.title: SeLMRoute: Probabilistic Semantic Evidence for Large Language Model Routing
paper-2609.34736.summary: Large language model (LLM) routing aims to select the most suitable model for each incoming query. Most existing routers learn this decision directly from query embeddings, model representations, preference data, or clusters of similar examples.

paper-2609.34826.title: WM-VLM: Probing Internal World Models for Interleaved Visual-Textual Reasoning
paper-2609.34826.summary: Humans often solve spatial problems by mentally simulating visual transformations. In contrast, conventional vision-language models (VLMs) reason primarily through language.

paper-2609.34895.title: LVMT: Video Mask Transformer for Long-term Video Segmentation
paper-2609.34895.summary: Existing online video segmentation methods struggle to track objects in long, complex videos with long-term occlusions.

paper-2609.34970.title: See it, Say it, Sorted: Mechanistic Diagnosis and Parameter-Space Mitigation of Emergent Misalignment in LLMs
paper-2609.34970.summary: Safety-aligned LLMs can exhibit emergent misalignment (EM): narrow domain adaptation unexpectedly triggers catastrophic safety failures across unrelated domains.

paper-2609.35259.title: On-Policy or Off-Policy Learning? A Systematic Study of Distillation Dynamics
paper-2609.35259.summary: On-policy learning has been argued to reduce catastrophic forgetting, produce sparser parameter updates, and improve generalisation.

paper-2609.35291.title: Narrow Multimodal Fine-Tuning Can Induce Emergent Misalignment
paper-2609.35291.summary: Modern AI models are aligned through post-training to adapt them to downstream tasks. Recent work shows that fine-tuning language models on narrow tasks can induce emergent misalignment (EM), causing broadly harmful behaviors beyond the training task.

paper-2609.35378.title: Multilinguality in Hybrid Attention LLMs
paper-2609.35378.summary: In response to the growing demand for long sequences in agentic and reasoning use cases, many state-of-the-art LLMs combine multiple variants of attention to mitigate the quadratic complexity of traditional softmax attention.

paper-2609.35433.title: ReSPO: Reshaped Sequence Policy Optimization for Gradient Starvation in Off-Policy Learning
paper-2609.35433.summary: Reinforcement learning from verifiable rewards (RLVR) frequently reuses rollouts across multiple policy updates, increasing the mismatch between the current policy and the data-generating policy.

paper-2609.35646.title: Rubric Rewards from Item Response Theory
paper-2609.35646.summary: Many language tasks have no single answer that can be checked automatically. Rubrics provide criteria for judging responses to these tasks. For reinforcement learning, the resulting verdicts must be combined into a scalar reward.

paper-2609.35652.title: MM-ABC: Towards Generalist Mobile Manipulation via Seeing, Coordinating and Imagining
paper-2609.35652.summary: Mobile manipulation extends robot interaction beyond a fixed kinematic workspace by making the reachable region itself controllable.

paper-2609.35690.title: Agent Priors-guided Policy Learning
paper-2609.35690.summary: Robots that learn from a few demonstrations often require two forms of generalization. Compositional generalization recombines skills to solve new tasks, and skill generalization lets the learned policy behind each skill work in new situations.

paper-2609.35751.title: How to Loop MoE: Flatten the Experts, Untie the Attention
paper-2609.35751.summary: Looped Transformers reuse one block of layers several times: by spending extra computation they push a model of fixed size further, and so use its parameters more fully; while sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) models activate only a few of many experts for each…

paper-2609.35855.title: Mara Chain: Rethinking Failure as a Stepping Stone for AI System Auto-Evolution
paper-2609.35855.summary: Optimizing deployed AI systems increasingly amounts to editing prompts, skills, harnesses, and code rather than model weights.

paper-2609.35922.title: Almost Human, Except When It Matters: VoxParity and the Decisions a Voice Should Change
paper-2609.35922.summary: A voice agent can handle almost every call on the words alone and still fail the few its sector's rules were written for.

paper-2609.35928.title: Prompted Identity Degrades Cooperation in Multi-Agent LLM Systems
paper-2609.35928.summary: Multi-agent LLM systems increasingly mix models from several providers, yet exposing each agent's underlying model identity to its peers significantly impairs cooperation.

paper-2609.35965.title: Systematic Multi-Agent Vision-and-Language Navigation: Formulation, Benchmark, and Method
paper-2609.35965.summary: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) has largely focused on a single agent following a single instruction, yet many real-world applications require teams of robots to tackle tasks beyond the capabilities of any individual agent.

paper-2609.36099.title: Data Unlearning via Inverse Distillation
paper-2609.36099.summary: Multi-step matching models, including flow and diffusion models, produce high-quality outputs but incur substantial inference costs and may reproduce unwanted components of their training datasets.

paper-2609.36138.title: When Does Correction Become Repair? Mechanistic Auditing of Internal Interventions in Tool-Using LLMs
paper-2609.36138.summary: Before invoking external tools, an agentic LLM must select among a K-way action space: executing a call, seeking clarification, answering directly, or declining.

paper-2609.36308.title: CheatBench: Measuring Reward Gaming in AI Agents
paper-2609.36308.summary: Reinforcement learning has helped AI agents solve increasingly difficult tasks, but high rewards do not always reflect the work users intended.

paper-2609.36333.title: ATLAS: Aligned Transport of Latent Structure for Reliable World Model Planning
paper-2609.36333.summary: Latent world models rely on representation geometry for planning, yet regularizing the latent marginal alone does not determine the state-to-state relationships used for action selection.

paper-2609.36388.title: Persona Dosing: Calibrated Activation Steering for Graded Trait Control
paper-2609.36388.summary: An activation-steering coefficient sets intervention strength, but requesting a particular degree of persona expression requires a behavioral scale.

paper-2609.36435.title: MemFold: Learning Compact Soft Memory for Long-Context Personalization via On-Policy Optimization
paper-2609.36435.summary: An assistant that serves the same user over a long horizon has to answer from what that user has revealed: which preferences still hold, which were revised, and which constraints apply now.

paper-2609.36484.title: The Teacher Is a Direction, Not a Destination: Extrapolating RL-Induced Representation Residuals in On-Policy Distillation
paper-2609.36484.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student to match the teacher's next-token distributions on the student's own trajectories and has yielded substantial empirical gains.

paper-2609.36529.title: Triadic Linear Attention: Three-Dimensional Recurrent States for Long-Context Sequence Modeling
paper-2609.36529.summary: Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) compress the historical context into a memory state of fixed size, thus allowing for constant-time inference.

paper-2609.36585.title: Transformers Stop Thinking Too Early, and a Tiny LoRA Fixes It
paper-2609.36585.summary: Pretrained transformers use little of their depth to follow references in context. Thirteen base models reliably follow only 1.4-3.6 lines, and extra pretrained loops add little.

paper-2609.36602.title: OTRetarget: Joint Robot and Object Motion Retargeting via Optimal Transport
paper-2609.36602.summary: Transferring human motion to humanoid robots requires adapting the demonstrated motion to the robot morphology while preserving interactions with the environment.

paper-2609.36616.title: CrossTimeEdit: A Decade-Spanning Cross-View Dataset and Reward-Guided Editing for Historical Street-View Generation
paper-2609.36616.summary: Historical street-view imagery records urban evolution, but uneven coverage leaves substantial gaps in historical records. Generating plausible past appearances requires restoring changed structures while preserving persistent scene content.

paper-2609.36641.title: Inducing Process Supervision from Outcome-Only Reinforcement Learning
paper-2609.36641.summary: Process reward models (PRMs) have become a key component for LLMs, as their step-level feedback supports both post-training and test-time reasoning.

paper-2609.36642.title: PR-OPD: Privileged Representation On-policy Self-Distillation for Agentic Reinforcement Learning
paper-2609.36642.summary: Language-model agents are usually trained by reinforcement learning from one reward per episode, and privileged self-distillation enriches it by letting the same policy, given a skill, teach its skill-free self through token probabilities.

paper-2609.36659.title: On-Policy Parameter Update Direction Underlies Generalization in LLM Post-Training
paper-2609.36659.summary: The strong generalization performance of on-policy post-training paradigms has motivated studies of their parameter update behaviors.

paper-2609.36684.title: ProgressCompass: Embodied Progress Reward Models Are Lost Without the Right Context
paper-2609.36684.summary: Embodied agents now take on ever longer tasks. For long tasks, knowing only whether a task finally succeeds or fails says little; the steps along the way matter.

paper-2609.36691.title: Video2Skill: From Streaming Experience to Reusable Embodied Skills
paper-2609.36691.summary: Manipulation behaviors vary widely across objects and scenes, but they share a small set of reusable skills, and planning with these skills helps embodied agents generalize to new tasks. Yet an agent can only plan with skills it knows.

paper-2609.36760.title: QuantMLA: Function-Aligned Dual-Path Quantization for Low-Bit MLA KV Caching
paper-2609.36760.summary: Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA) enables expressive multi-head attention with compact caches for its content and decoupled RoPE paths, yet cache memory still scales linearly with context length and batch size.

paper-2609.36820.title: CorrGRPO: Correlation-Normalized GRPO for Multi-Reward Learning
paper-2609.36820.summary: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) is widely used to train reasoning language models, where it computes advantages by centering and normalizing rewards across rollouts of the same prompt.

paper-2609.36887.title: WEFT: Scaling Tool-Use Post-Training for General-Purpose Agents
paper-2609.36887.summary: Recent efforts to scale tool-use post-training have largely centered on the synthesis of executable environments, which constitute only one component of a broader agentic interaction system comprising the environment, task, agent harness, and evaluator.

paper-2609.36931.title: Dating the Model: Hidden Dates in System Prompts Affect LLM Evaluation
paper-2609.36931.summary: Reproducibility is essential for scientific research, yet prior work shows that LLM outputs vary with hardware and batching.

paper-2609.36956.title: Controlled Decoding Attacks on Black-Box LLMs
paper-2609.36956.summary: Manipulating next-token probabilities during generation can bypass the safety alignment of large language models.

paper-2609.36995.title: Salt++: Context-Aligned Post-Training for Few-Step Streaming Multimodal Generation
paper-2609.36995.summary: Few-step streaming audio--video generation requires both causal modeling and step distillation, yet standard training recipes face two context-related challenges.

paper-2609.37200.title: Adaptive Reward Routing: Dynamic Multi-Reward Optimization for Joint Audio-Video Diffusion via Forward-Process RL
paper-2609.37200.summary: Multi-reward guided reinforcement learning (i.e., RL) offers a promising way to improve joint audio-video diffusion models along several complementary objectives, including modality-specific quality, cross-modal semantic alignment, and temporal synchronizatio…

paper-2609.37267.title: Foundations of Proactive Agents: Principles, Technical Layers, and Proactivity-Gym
paper-2609.37267.summary: Proactive LLM agents can turn idle compute into useful support before users ask. Yet even correct work can misread user context, impose review costs, or undermine trust.

paper-2609.37334.title: Taming VLAs under Robot Execution Errors: Self-Compensation and Stress Testing

paper-2610.19138.summary: How well can a language model turn a large, incomplete and partly contradictory body of documents into a plan when no single correct answer exists?

paper-2610.19361.title: VLX-Go: Robust Embodied Tracking through Multi-Stage Learning and On-Policy Refinement
paper-2610.19361.summary: Embodied visual tracking requires a robot to identify a designated target from visual observations and control its own motion to follow that target through an environment.

paper-2610.19366.title: Seeing, Maintaining, and Learning: The Evolution of Multimodal Agent Memory
paper-2610.19366.summary: Multimodal models and agents have emerged to enable AI systems to learn from and interact with the real world more like humans by integrating information across multiple modalities.

paper-2610.19420.title: From Failures to Learnable Worlds: Policy-Conditioned Environment Generation for Navigation Agents
paper-2610.19420.summary: Simulated environments enable scalable training data generation for embodied agents, but more data does not necessarily provide what a particular agent needs to learn.

paper-2610.19422.title: AgentSafeEvo: Adversarial Co-Evolution for LLM Agent Safety
paper-2610.19422.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents accomplish complex tasks through multi-turn interactions with external tools.

paper-2610.19525.title: Diagnosing and Correcting Reward Hacking in Verifiable Instruction Following
paper-2610.19525.summary: Verifiable instruction-following benchmarks emphasize output-constraint satisfaction but can overlook whether responses meaningfully answer the underlying request, creating an evaluation blind spot.

paper-2610.19551.title: TextVerifier: Seeing Beyond Recognition to Verify Chinese Text Rendering
paper-2610.19551.summary: Text-to-image models increasingly generate readable Chinese text that still contains local rendering defects, such as a character with an extra or missing stroke or a malformed component.

paper-2610.19560.title: τ-Emotion-Bench: Exposing the Interaction Fragility of LLM Agents through Real-World User Emotions
paper-2610.19560.summary: In long-horizon tool-calling tasks, LLM agents can fail not only because of tool-use errors, but also because of ineffective interaction with users.

paper-2610.19628.title: Self-Conditioning Enables Deep Sequential Reasoning in Flow Matching
paper-2610.19628.summary: Recent work has explored visual reasoning through image generation, where models solve visual-reasoning problems by directly generating solution images.

paper-2610.19696.title: Share the Symbol, Not the Vector: Training-Free Fact Communication Across Language Models
paper-2610.19696.summary: Multi-agent systems allow language models to solve tasks collaboratively by sharing complementary information. These systems typically communicate through text, while recent approaches also explore exchanging internal model states.

paper-2610.19698.title: RuleTrek: Benchmarking Agentic Rule Reasoning in Complex Scenarios
paper-2610.19698.summary: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly tackle complex real-world tasks in specialized domains. However, identifying and correctly applying domain-specific rules remains challenging when scenario information is distributed across multiple files.

paper-2610.19726.title: Generative World Simulation with DAO and JING
paper-2610.19726.summary: We present a Generative World Simulation framework that couples persistent shared world state with continuous first-person audiovisual generation.

paper-2610.19729.title: A Diagnostic Study of World-Space Human Recovery Under High Camera Dynamics
paper-2610.19729.summary: Monocular world-space human recovery methods excel on current benchmarks, but these rarely include fast camera motion. We introduce the K-Pop stress test, broadcast dance videos that combine fast, large camera motion with dense multi-person choreography.

paper-2610.19789.title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
paper-2610.19789.summary: Self-distillation in agentic reinforcement learning has produced a growing number of methods.

paper-2610.19820.title: ActionOPD: Distilling Decisions, Not Tokens
paper-2610.19820.summary: Distilling capable language-model agents into smaller models requires aligning the student's behavior with the teacher's. This raises a fundamental question: at which states and at what granularity should this alignment be performed?

paper-2610.19975.title: LatentLoop: Scaling Looped MoE Models with Asymmetric Compute Allocation
paper-2610.19975.summary: Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models combine parameter reuse with sparse computation to improve performance under matched budgets. Prior work demonstrates that different loop visits can play different roles even when they share parameters.

paper-2610.20137.title: StreamErase: Towards Ultra-Fast Streaming Video Erasing
paper-2610.20137.summary: Current video object removal methods suffer from prohibitive latency (minutes per video) and non-causal processing that prevents real-time interaction. We present StreamErase, enabling sub-second latency with up to 26 FPS streaming generation on a single GPU.

paper-2610.20195.title: What Makes a Social Agent's Interactions Effective? Learning from Verifiable Outcomes in Paired Worlds
paper-2610.20195.summary: Effective social interaction requires more than fluent responses: agents must reach plans that fit the participants' needs and circumstances.

paper-2610.20220.title: Glance Forcing: Making Bidirectional Diffusion Autoregressive at a Glance
paper-2610.20220.summary: Autoregressive generation underlies real-time, causal video synthesis and is the backbone of video world models.

paper-2610.20256.title: Long-Horizon RL Needs Muon
paper-2610.20256.summary: Long-horizon agents must coordinate reasoning, tool use, and environment feedback over extended interactions.

paper-2610.20344.title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
paper-2610.20344.summary: Agents driven by large language models are increasingly deployed on long-horizon tasks, where they use tools and modify real workspaces. How well they perform depends as much on the harness around the model as on the model itself.

paper-2610.20399.title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory
paper-2610.20399.summary: Context can improve large language model performance, but these gains may be lost after context removal.

paper-2610.20431.title: SwarmRSI: Recursive Self-Improvement through Evolving Scientific Agent Swarm
paper-2610.20431.summary: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) in scientific research aims to improve agents' research capabilities through their own experimental experience.

paper-2610.20442.title: Towards Agentic Robots: Model, Data, Environment, and Harness
paper-2610.20442.summary: Foundation models are driving a paradigm shift in robotic intelligence, moving beyond low-level action prediction to goal-directed orchestration of data collection, model training, task planning, and real-world execution.

paper-2610.20456.title: The COUNT: Counting N-grams Unlocks Scaling on Host Memory and Training-Free Adaptation
paper-2610.20456.summary: The scaling relationship of compute and performance for language models (LMs) has been extensively studied; more recently, models are being designed to scale memory use, as well.

paper-2610.20516.title: VASPO: Self-Distillation with Privileged Value Estimation
paper-2610.20516.summary: On-policy self-distillation provides dense supervision for reasoning models via a privileged self-teacher. However, this supervision reflects local token preferences rather than the expected return of an unguided student continuation.

paper-2610.20524.title: Physical Time as a Missing Dimension of Robot Policy Memory Dynamics
paper-2610.20524.summary: Existing robot policy memories typically evolve with observation sequences, implicitly treating each update as the same amount of physical time.

paper-2610.20526.title: Lluna: Collaborative Unimodal Models for Missing-Modality Inference
paper-2610.20526.summary: Pretrained unimodal models offer a flexible route to multimodal prediction through collaboration, but this collaboration can become less accurate than a surviving unimodal model when modalities are missing.

paper-2610.20571.title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
paper-2610.20571.summary: Long-form agentic video generation must turn a screenplay into shots that remain spatially and temporally consistent across nonconsecutive requests.

paper-2610.20572.title: Recovering Reliable Supervision via Critique-Guided On-Policy Distillation
paper-2610.20572.summary: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a student model on its own rollouts with token-level supervision from a teacher, assuming that the teacher can reach a correct answer from any prefix the student writes.

paper-2610.20582.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
paper-2610.20582.summary: Long contexts enlarge key--value (KV) caches, increasing memory use and attention costs during generation. Compressing these caches must preserve information for unseen questions.

paper-2610.20584.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
paper-2610.20584.summary: Computer-use agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in interpreting screens and executing keyboard and mouse actions.

paper-2610.20586.title: Continuum Attention
paper-2610.20586.summary: We introduce Continuum Attention (CA), a causal Transformer attention operator that replaces discrete key and value lookup with integration over a continuous, piecewise linear memory curve. Each query induces an exponential relevance density along the curve.

paper-2610.20588.title: Your Transformer Is Secretly Elastic
paper-2610.20588.summary: Scaling up transformers has produced models with broad capabilities, deployed across heterogeneous hardware and fluctuating workloads.

paper-2610.20604.title: VITAL: From Visual Motion to Precise Action
paper-2610.20604.summary: World-action models aim to turn visual anticipation into driving decisions, yet typically train action experts on trajectory representations defined independently of visual dynamics. This motivates deriving action targets directly from visual motion.

paper-2610.20609.title: SafeDriveVLA: Navigation-Conditioned World Model Dreaming for Conflict-Aware End-to-End Autonomous Driving
paper-2610.20609.summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models are gaining attention in autonomous driving, inheriting commonsense priors from large language models (LLMs) and widening the navigation interface from a fixed command set to free-form natural-language instructions.
